title: Development Finance LTV, LTC & LTGDV Explained
summary: Blog article (not a case study). Thesis: three lending metrics set how much a developer can borrow on a development loan - loan-to-value (LTV, the loan against the site's current value), loan-to-cost (LTC, the loan against total project cost including land, build and fees) and loan-to-gross-development-value (LTGDV, the loan against the projected completed value). The article says these metrics directly affect the maximum loan available, the equity the developer must contribute and whether the project is financially viable. Concrete guidance revealed: two worked examples - a GBP 5m site with a GBP 3m day-one advance = 60% LTV, and a GBP 4m completed scheme with a GBP 2.8m facility = 70% LTGDV; LTV is said to be most relevant when the developer plans to purchase the site first or refinance an existing facility secured on the site; LTC is described as typically up to 85%-90%. Sibling Silver Oak pages surfaced by the same search add market caps (senior lenders usually cap at 65%-70% of GDV; 75% LTGDV / 90% LTC usually applies to residential schemes with commercial capped lower; lenders generally not above 90%-95% LTC; land without planning unlikely to secure over 50% LTV; stretch senior up to 75% GDV or 90% LTC at a blended 8%-10% p.a. plus execution fees) and note that lenders heavily scrutinise the borrower's equity contribution. The full article text, H1, meta description, author, publication date, section headings, FAQ and calls to action were NOT revealed by the search results.

[b] "LTC (loan to cost) is the loan against total project cost, including land, build, and fees. Typically up to 85% – 90%."

notes: Direct fetching was blocked; everything above comes from two WebSearch 'extended' calls on 2026-10-29: [a] the exact URL, [b] 'site:silveroakcapital.co.uk development finance LTV LTC LTGDV lenders borrow'. Neither returned the full article; the search tool itself said it had only excerpts. Confirmed as the article's own content by both searches: the thesis (three metrics set borrowing capacity; they drive max loan, equity requirement and viability), the GBP 5m / GBP 3m = 60% LTV example, and (from [a] only) the GBP 4m / GBP 2.8m = 70% LTGDV example. Items from [b] attributed to sibling pages (senior development page, FAQ, requirements article, stretch senior page, post-planning land page) are recorded with their attribution and may NOT appear in the article itself; the '85%-90% LTC' line and the 'equity contribution' line were attributed by the search summary to Silver Oak pages generally without naming the page. NOT revealed: H1 (the slug suggests a longer title ending 'How Lenders Decide What You Can Borrow', but this is inferred from the URL, not seen), meta description, author, publication date, section headings, FAQ block, calls to action, images. The 'sections' field is a thematic grouping of revealed content, not confirmed headings. Third-party definitions and caps returned by search [a] (Kuflink, Brickflow/land.tech, Property Tax Partners, thefinancebrokers.co.uk, FD Commercial, Statuskwo, Doulton Bridging - e.g. 'lender advances the lower of the two figures', 'first-time developers often 85% LTC and 65% LTGDV') were deliberately excluded as they are not Silver Oak content. The seed file's one-line note for this URL (LTV = loan / current value; LTC = loan / total development cost; LTGDV = loan / GDV) is consistent with what was found. The search tool's '114 to 213 days old' dating refers to Silver Oak pages generally, not specifically this article.
